COSTERMONGER GUISE.

An up-to-date four-in-hand, with donkeys in the place of horses, a costermonger's barrow as a vehicle, and three costermongers as occupants, will take the road from London to Epsom at nine o'clock this morning.
This novel equipage will start—as the result of a bet—from a London hotel, and, wending its way out of London, will mingle with the vast stream of traffic en route for Epsom.

Arrived at the course, its occupants—coster-mongers of the deepest dye!—will alight and enter a large closed motor-car, whence they will issue later on in the attire of average, well-to-do English-men!

The perpetrators of this prank are three officers in a well-known cavity regime, and they are journeying in this guise and fashion to the races in order to win a very tempting bet. The company's management

The wager was offered by their brother-officers, who dare them—at 20 to 1 odds—to drive a four-in-hand coter's donkey barrow on Derby Day from a London hotel to the racecourse at Epsom, each of them to be clad as a typical coter.

The wager was promptly taken by three officers, who at once began preparations. First,
First, a genuine two-wheeled costermonger's barrow, capable of seating four persons and being pulled by two donkeys, was hired.

By an ingenious contrivance in the shape of an iron bar attached to the shafts provision was made for two more donkeys, and it only remained to hire four donkeys—three light grey and one brown—from various costers to make this novel four-in-hand complete.

There were still the costumes to be considered, and, that everything might be quite "de rigueur," the three officers placed themselves in the hands of a well-known theatrical costumer, who will metamorphose them into jersey-clad, blue-chinned costers of the most realistic type.
